name: DISA STIG, SSH server (macOS 15)
reference: CIS Apple macOS 15 (Sequoia) STIG Benchmark v1.0.0, the rule 'SSHD must be configured to limit the Ciphers, HostbasedAcceptedAlgorithms, HostKeyAlgorithms, KexAlgorithms, MACs, PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms and CASignatureAlgorithms to FIPS-compliant connections'. The audit builds a fips_sshd_config array and fails a server that offers anything not on it, so this profile is an allowlist taken verbatim from that array.
summary: The US Department of Defense hardening for SSH on macOS 15, as the STIG spells it out: a very tight FIPS allowlist built around P-256. Only aes128-gcm, ecdh-sha2-nistp256, HMAC-SHA-256 and ECDSA-P-256 host keys conform; everything else fails.
notes: An allowlist, like the RHEL 9 STIG and unlike CIS, but far narrower: the macOS STIG pins a single cipher (aes128-gcm@openssh.com), a single key exchange (ecdh-sha2-nistp256), two MACs (hmac-sha2-256 in its EtM and plain forms) and ECDSA over P-256 for host keys. A server offering aes256-gcm, curve25519, chacha20 or an Ed25519 host key fails, even though those are strong -- the point of the profile is to measure against what the STIG mandates, not against what is good. The lists are taken verbatim from the audit's fips_sshd_config array. The STIG also constrains PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms, HostbasedAcceptedAlgorithms and CASignatureAlgorithms to the same P-256 set, but those classes are about how a client authenticates, not what the server advertises in the key exchange, so the scanner does not observe them and this profile states no rule for them. As with disa-stig-rhel-9-ssh, this is the macOS 15 STIG specifically: DISA STIG SSH crypto differs by platform, so other platforms are separate profiles rather than editions of this one.

cipher.reason: The fips_sshd_config array names exactly this one cipher.

kex.reason: The fips_sshd_config array names exactly this one key exchange (ECDH over P-256).

mac.reason: The fips_sshd_config array names exactly these two MACs.

host_key.reason: The fips_sshd_config array's HostKeyAlgorithms names exactly these four, all ECDSA over P-256.
